string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People\'s Republic of China and one of its four direct-administered municipalities. Located in the north of the country, it has served as the national capital for more than eight hundred years, leaving a legacy of imperial palaces, temples and gardens. Landmarks such as the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven and sections of the nearby Great Wall are recognised as UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Today Beijing is the country\'s political, cultural and educational centre, home to over twenty-one million people, leading universities and numerous company headquarters. In 2008 and 2022 it became the first city to host both the Summer and Winter Olympic Games.

Shanghai is China\'s largest city and a leading global financial centre, situated on the eastern coast where the Yangtze River meets the East China Sea. The Huangpu River divides the city into two contrasting areas: the historic Bund with its colonial-era buildings and the futuristic skyline of Pudong, crowned by the Oriental Pearl Tower. Shanghai became a direct-administered municipality in 1927 and grew rapidly into the country\'s commercial and industrial heart. Its port is among the busiest in the world, handling enormous volumes of cargo and containers. With a population of about twenty-five million, the city blends traditional neighbourhoods, such as the Yu Garden area, with striking modern architecture.

Chongqing is a direct-administered municipality in south-western China and the largest of the four by area, covering about 82,000 square kilometres. Known as the Mountain City, it stands at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers, and its steep terrain produces a striking skyline of bridges, stairs and hillside buildings. Originally part of Sichuan Province, it was granted municipality status in 1997 to help develop the western regions and administer the Three Gorges Dam area. Chongqing is a major centre of manufacturing, especially automobiles and motorcycles. It is also famous for its spicy hot pot, frequent fog, and vibrant night views along the river.

Tianjin is a northern coastal municipality that borders Beijing and Hebei Province, serving as the main seaport for the capital region. The name means \"Heaven\'s Ford\" and was granted by the Yongle Emperor of the Ming dynasty in 1404, when the city became a walled garrison. During the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries Tianjin was opened as a treaty port, and the former British, French, Italian and other concessions left a legacy of distinctive European-style architecture. Today the city is an important industrial, financial and shipping centre, and Tianjin Port is one of the largest ports in the world. Modern landmarks include the Tianjin Eye, a Ferris wheel built on a bridge.
